subject: Request: Clarify streaming vs non-streaming SLA — first-token budget and sustained rate profile
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@bankcorp.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: BankCorp Procurement <procurement@bankcorp.com>
Date: 2025-10-09T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Clarification: streaming TTFT vs sustained throughput for holiday traffic

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency profiling. We need a tighter set of commitments on streaming endpoints before procurement can sign. Two specific asks:

1) Time-to-first-token (TTFT) expectations for streaming endpoints. Our production UX requires TTFT <= 300ms p95 in normal conditions, but we expect many short sessions during peak (holiday campaign) where the first-token matters more than sustained throughput.

2) Sustained token/sec profile: we have workloads that spike to ~3k tokens/sec for short bursts (tens of seconds) but average ~200–400 tok/sec per endpoint. We need to understand how Redwood would guarantee sustained rate vs allowburst handling.

Is there an exception path to increase short-term burst allowance for streaming endpoints without triggering full dedicated capacity pricing? We're open to a pilot. Attaching a sample trace and procurement timeline.

Also, procurement asked whether Redwood can offer an explicit "first-token budget" — i.e., a capped number of calls per billing period that get stronger TTFT guarantees (higher priority queue) to cover campaign bursts.

Can you propose concrete options? We need to finalize commercial terms by Oct 24.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Senior SRE — BankCorp

Attachments: burst_profile_samples.csv (csv), pilot-rollout-timeline.pdf (pdf)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-09T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Clarification: streaming TTFT vs sustained throughput for holiday traffic

Folks — forwarding BankCorp's note. They want explicit options for TTFT and a burst allowance that doesn't force Dedicated. Draft below; please review and add numbers we can commit to. Key constraints: we need to protect other tenants and not overpromise on endemic burst patterns. Proposed approach: 

- First-token budget: configurable allotment (e.g., N calls/month) that route into a high-priority streaming queue. Suggested pilot: 250k prioritized calls/month for the first 30 days, with p95 TTFT target of <= 300ms on that subset.

- Sustained rate profile: guaranteed baseline (e.g., 400 tok/sec sustained per endpoint) with a short burst buffer of +2.5x for up to 30s per minute, applied proportionally across tenants. Bursts beyond buffer fall back to either slower token emission (degraded SLO) or automatic fallback to our non-streaming endpoint which provides full response but higher TTFC.

- Pricing construct: a small monthly surcharge for the prioritized budget (applied only if >50% utilization). Otherwise, include pilot at no uplift to get them signed.

Questions for Rishi: can we commit to p95 TTFT <=300ms for the prioritized calls during pilot given BankCorp's expected mix? And what telemetry/alerts will we provide so they can measure compliance?

I'll draft a short client-facing reply once we agree numbers.

—Olga
Account Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachment (for internal): BankCorp_SLA_Redlines_v3.docx (redlines)

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@bankcorp.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-10T11:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarification: streaming TTFT vs sustained throughput for holiday traffic

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. Below are two practical options we can offer; each includes SLAs, rollback behavior, and measurement hooks. Pick the one you prefer and we will attach formal redlines.

Option A — Prioritized Streaming (recommended pilot)
- First-token budget: Redwood will reserve a prioritized queue for up to 250k calls/month (pilot). Calls in the prioritized queue receive p95 TTFT <= 300ms measured at the edge.
- Sustained rate: baseline guarantee of 400 tok/sec sustained per endpoint with a burst buffer of up to 2.5x (i.e., up to 1000 tok/sec) for bursts lasting no more than 30s per occurrence and no more than 10% of total monthly active minutes.
- Degradation policy: if buffer is exceeded we will gracefully degrade token emission to preserve fairness; fallback to non-streaming (synchronous) endpoint is available as a configured fallback with p99 response completion targets but higher first-byte latency.
- Observability: we will deliver a per-call tag for prioritized traffic, a 1-minute aggregated telemetry feed, and weekly TTFT/tokens/sec reports.
- Pricing: pilot month included at no uplift; subsequent months: small usage surcharge for prioritized budget if >50% utilized.

Option B — Hybrid Fallback (conservative)
- No prioritized budget. Instead Redwood will guarantee 250 tok/sec baseline with automatic, policy-driven short-term scaling to preemptively route heavy bursts to (1) a non-streaming fallback endpoint or (2) a temporary dedicated burst pool (if enabled) with explicit pricing.
- TTFT for streaming calls under this plan is p95 <= 400ms under typical conditions; during burst fallback TTFT may exceed 500ms.

Risks and notes:
- Our p95 TTFT guarantee requires realistic sequence-length distribution. Extremely short prompts (very latency-sensitive) should be captured in the prioritized budget.
- The burst buffer is shared across tenants; if multiple tenants spike simultaneously the effective headroom shrinks. For absolute isolation we recommend Dedicated capacity.

If you want, we can increase the prioritized budget to 500k calls/month for an incremental fee or grant a seasonal burst uplift (e.g., +5% for defined holiday windows). I attached a redline with the exact SLA language.

Append: excerpt of proposed SLA redline and the pilot timeline.

Subject: Re: Clarification: streaming TTFT vs sustained throughput for holiday traffic

Rishi/Olga — thank you, that is exactly the structure procurement and SRE needed. We prefer Option A with two small changes before sign:

1) Increase the prioritized call budget to 350k calls/month for the pilot (we expect several campaign waves).
2) Add a seasonal burst uplift clause: allow a one-time +10% burst buffer during a 14-day predefined holiday window (we will give 30 days notice).

If you can confirm those two tweaks we will circulate to procurement and aim to execute the amendment by Oct 22. Also, please include the telemetry feed (1-min aggregated) so my team can validate TTFT during the pilot.

Thanks — looking forward to the pilot.

Alex Turner
Senior SRE — BankCorp
